- For trace IDs / request IDs: would Redwood pseudonymize or hash these when storing logs so we can still correlate without storing raw IDs?
- What retention windows are configurable for request logs and KV/response caches? Our default policy is 30 days, but we need options down to 7 days for sensitive routes.

Hi Alice — great talking earlier, and thanks for the detailed list. High-level answers below and a proposed next step. I've attached a short design doc (redaction_design_v1.pdf) that outlines our current redaction capabilities and configuration knobs.

Summary answers (short):
- Default logging: By default our hosted API collects metadata (timestamps, model, route, latencies) and minimal request metadata (method, route, status). Request/response bodies are NOT stored by default for standard customer configs on hosted tier. For Dedicated/Private we allow per-customer controls; request/response body logging is optional and can be disabled per-route.
- Headers: We maintain a configurable header allowlist. Out-of-the-box we retain: user-agent, x-cloud-region, x-model, x-request-duration. We explicitly strip Authorization and cookie headers. You can supply a custom allowlist/denylist per-tenant.
- PII redaction: We support several modes: none, pattern-based redaction, schema-based redaction (field-level), and tokenization/hashing. Redaction can be applied at the ingress gateway (closest to SDK), or at the storage layer before persisting logs. For minimal exposure we recommend gateway-side redaction + storage-layer verification.
- Trace IDs: We support pseudonymization (SHA-256 with per-tenant salt) for trace IDs before storage so correlation is possible but raw IDs are not retained. We can also optionally store a reversible mapping in private deployments if you need re-identification for debugging (audit-only with access controls).
- Retention: Retention windows are configurable per data class and per-route. Defaults are 90 days for non-sensitive logs, 30 days for request metadata, with options down to 7 days for sensitive routes. We can support 7/14/30/90 day buckets and automated lifecycle policies.

Recommended next steps:
1) We can run a 30-minute technical sync next Tue (6/30) or Wed (7/1) to review the attached design and map your sensitive routes.
2) If you can share a small sample log schema or a redaction mapping (field->PII type) we can produce a proposed configuration and sample sanitized logs.
3) We'll provide a short config YAML and an implementation timeline (2 weeks for standard routes, 3-4 weeks for complex integrations).

I've CC'd Rishi (solutions) to propose a timeline and dev ask.

Hi team — looping in a couple technical details from our infra/serving side. Forwarding Marissa's note below for context.

Quick tech notes:
- Pattern redaction: we use RE2-safe regex patterns for SSNs/CCNs and a library of PII detectors for names/emails. Pattern redaction runs at the gateway with backoff to avoid perf impacts.
- Schema redaction: if you provide a JSON schema or sample payloads we can configure field-level redaction (e.g., payload.user.email -> mask, payload.payment.card_number -> truncate-last4+hash).
- Trace IDs: by default we salt-and-hash trace IDs (configurable salt per-tenant). For high-cardinality tracing we recommend keeping an ephemeral mapping in a secure key-value store with strict RBAC; otherwise hashed IDs are sufficient for incident correlation.
- Audit logs: every redaction/hashing event is itself logged to an audit trail (who/what/when) and retained per your retention policy — configurable separately from request logs.

Dev note: we'll need a small sample (10-20 requests across ~3 routes) and an example of what you consider PII in each payload. Can you drop that into the Drive link above or send via secure upload?

Timeline: given the sample schema and a 30-minute sync, we can produce a config and sanitized sample logs within 2 business days. Full rollout (testing + canary) for 3-5 routes typically takes 2 weeks.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
